title: UAE Issues Emergency Missile Alert, Urges Residents to Seek Shelter
excerpt: The UAE defence ministry detected potential missile threats on Monday, issuing emergency alerts before authorities confirmed the situation was safe.
body:
• UAE defence ministry detected potential missile threats Monday, triggering emergency phone alerts across the country
  • Residents were told to immediately seek shelter in secure buildings and await further instructions
  • Authorities later confirmed the situation was safe and urged people to resume normal activities with caution
  • UAE ambassador stated the country will not participate in any attacks on Iran amid the ongoing regional conflict

The United Arab Emirates defence ministry on Monday detected potential missile threats and issued emergency alerts to residents' mobile phones, asking them to immediately seek shelter in secure buildings. The alert came amid heightened regional tensions from the ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran.

Within minutes, the UAE's interior ministry sent a follow-up notification confirming that the situation was safe and asking residents to resume normal activities "while continuing to remain cautious and take the necessary precautions," according to Reuters.

A Pattern of Alerts Amid Regional Conflict

Monday's alert was the latest in a series of missile warnings issued to UAE residents since the U.S.-Iran conflict began in late February. In May, authorities issued a similar alert that was later declared safe. In late June, the National Emergency Crisis and Disaster Management Authority (NCEMA) confirmed that a separate emergency warning had been triggered by a "sudden technical malfunction" in the early warning system.

Not all alerts have been false alarms. Earlier this year, UAE air defenses engaged actual missile attacks and incoming drones from Iran, according to Gulf Business. The defence ministry at the time confirmed its systems were intercepting ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and unmanned aerial vehicles, noting that explosions heard by residents were caused by interception operations rather than direct impacts.

UAE Seeks Diplomatic Distance From Conflict

In a notable diplomatic statement, the UAE ambassador emphasized that the country "will not partake in any attacks" on Iran, signaling Abu Dhabi's desire to maintain a separate position from the broader U.S.-led military campaign.

"UAE Air Defence systems are actively engaging with missiles and UAV threats."

— UAE Ministry of Defence, during a previous interception operation

The UAE hosts Al Dhafra Air Base, a key facility used by U.S. forces. The country has found itself caught between its security partnership with Washington and the need to avoid becoming a primary target. The Pentagon is separately considering relocating some Gulf bases farther from Iran's missile range, with Al Dhafra among the installations under review.

Millions of Indian Expats in the Line of Fire

The missile alerts carry particular weight for the estimated 3.5 million Indians living in the UAE, the largest expatriate community in the country. During previous alerts, the Indian embassy urged citizens to follow local safety guidance and shelter instructions.

The U.S. Embassy in Abu Dhabi has maintained a Level 3 "Reconsider Travel" advisory for the UAE since the start of the conflict, with routine visa services suspended and non-emergency government personnel relocated. Foreign missions from India, the United Kingdom, and the United States have all urged their nationals to stay vigilant.

What's Next

The frequency of missile alerts underscores the ongoing security risks in the Gulf, even as diplomatic efforts to end the U.S.-Iran conflict continue. A memorandum of understanding signed in June was intended to halt military operations and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but the ceasefire collapsed within weeks.

Washington currently maintains roughly 50,000 troops across the Middle East, including more than 20 warships. For UAE residents, the government's rapid alert-and-reassurance cycle has become a familiar pattern, testing the nerves of millions living under the shadow of the regional conflict.
nri_angle: Millions of Indian expats in the UAE face repeated security alerts as the Gulf region remains caught in the crossfire of the U.S.-Iran conflict.
author: Diaspora Desk
